naslov: Four Questions on the Day of Judgement

segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement. May blessings and peace be upon His beloved one, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

My dear brothers, I ask Him, the Exalted, to let us live in goodness (khayr). I ask Him, the Exalted, to grant us patience, to grant us health. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. My dear, respected brothers, this dunya (this world) – or rather man in this dunya – is like a traveller, like a wayfarer (musafir), who stays in it briefly and then continues on his way to his final destination.

And what is promised to man in the Qur'an will truly come, in the words of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala: "And what you are promised" – that you will give account on the Day of Judgement – "is the truth."

And each of us will give account before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, individually, as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا" – and each one will come to Him on the Day of Judgement – how?

Individually. Just imagine that scene: that you stand before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, only you and your Lord, and you give account for what you did in this dunya. A person's feet will not move on the day when he gives account until he is asked about several things, of which the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, also informs us, saying…
He says: a person's feet will not move from the place of reckoning until he is asked about several things.
In the first place, as the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions, he says, in the first place, he says, he will be asked about his lifespan, about his lifespan – how he spent it.

Did we spend our life, our lifespan, in obedience to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, or in disobedience? At the time when the muezzin calls us from the minaret: "Come to prayer", did we at that time pass by the mosque and go to some other place, which is much, much less important?
Were we obedient to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, or did we spend that time on unimportant things,

on unimportant things? Did we spend time on our family, or did we spend time in coffee houses, in taverns, in gambling dens, at pointless gatherings where people backbite one another, where haram is committed, and so on, and so on?

The time in which we were supposed to – having taken on a trust (amanah) – do a certain job that is useful for the community, did we just wait for that time to pass so we could go home, or did we do our job the way it should be done?

A person will not move his foot without giving, that is, without giving an answer to this question. The second thing the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions, he says: he will be asked about his knowledge – whether he acted upon it, whether he acted upon his knowledge, whether he acted upon what we know.

We know many things today, dear brothers, but we do not act upon them. Every Friday (jumu'ah) we hear from the minbar: "Brothers, a Muslim should perform the prayer. Brothers, a Muslim should give zakat. Brothers, a Muslim should fast. Brothers, a Muslim should love his brother and respect him.
Brothers, it is not permissible for a Muslim to take the right of his Muslim brother." Did we act upon what we know, or did we just do whatever we felt like?
In one ear and out the other. A Muslim must not be like that. Also, what a Muslim should do is seek knowledge, seek Islamic knowledge,

so that he knows how to worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. This is not only about what you know, but also about what you should know but don't, and many things. Also, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: he will be asked about money – how he acquired it, where he acquired it, whether he acquired it in a haram or halal way.

Today people can declare something halal or haram for themselves. He is told kindly: "Brother, that is haram for you." – "It is," he says, "halal." Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Wa la taqulu lima tasifu alsinatukumul-kadhiba hadha halalun wa hadha haramun li taftaru 'alallahil-kadhib."

And He says: do not utter lies with your tongues: "This is halal, this is haram", so as to lie and invent falsehoods against Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. "Innal-ladhina yaftaruna 'alallahil-kadhiba la yuflihun" – truly those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. "Mata'un qalil" – He says: it is only a brief enjoyment; a person declares something halal for himself in the dunya so that he can enjoy it briefly. "Mata'un qalilun wa lahum 'adhabun alim" – and, He says, a severe, painful torment awaits them.
So whoever declares halal or haram something that Allah has not declared halal or haram, woe to him, woe to him. That is why a person should be careful about how he earned his money.

It is not important, dear brothers, just to stuff our pockets. That is not what matters. What matters is – is it halal or haram? Will we feed our family with haram or with halal? Will we feed our family with money that was taken unjustly?
Will we feed our family from goods, haram goods, such as alcohol? Will we feed our family from wealth, or from money from gambling dens,

from interest (riba) and so on? For all of it we will be, for all of it we will be questioned. Pay attention, dear brothers: here the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, regarding what is connected to money, mentions two things: how a person acquired it
وَفِيمَ أَنْفَقَهُ
segmenti.prevod: “…and on what he spent it.” (part of a hadith, at-Tirmidhi)

segmenti.tekst: and where he spent it, where he spent it. Did he spend his money on his family, or on haram things: on drugs, gambling, alcohol,
amusements that destroy a person. He gets bored, he goes to haram places and spends his money in haram places. He says: "I earned that with my own ten fingers."

That is a falsehood, a great falsehood, dear brothers. You know yourselves how much a person sometimes strives, but there is no provision (nafaqa), and sometimes, with little work, a great deal of provision comes to a person.

So provision is from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. That is why a person should be careful where [unclear]. And finally the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "wa 'an jismihi fima ablahu" – and a person will be asked about his body: how he, how he used it, how he wore it out, in what way. Because this body, in which our soul resides, has only been given to us for use, only given to us for use in this dunya,

and sooner or later it will be returned to its Lord. Did we protect our body, did we protect our health from vices, alcohol, drugs? Did we… there are some trends now, and we see people cutting themselves with knives, and then, supposedly, that's now a thing, he's dangerous; and then we see people, we see these young people putting out cigarettes on their bodies, getting tattooed, and so on, and so on, or destroying their bodies with various vices.

For all of this a person, a person will be questioned. It, our body, has been given to us for use. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an: "وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ" [unclear] "إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا" [unclear]. And that is why a person should remember these five things well, five things. The first thing, as we said: that he will be asked about his lifespan.

The second thing is that he will be asked about his knowledge – whether he acted upon it. The third thing is that he will be asked about his money, and here we have two, two questions about money: how we earned it and where we spent it.
And finally, and finally, about his, about his body: a person will be asked about his body. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who fulfil their obligations towards their Lord.

To make us among those who give what is due to their Lord, to their Muslim brother, to their family, to their wife. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who give what is due [unclear], to make us among the God-fearing, to let us live in goodness. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us the sins of our parents and to gather us together in Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin.

بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لِي وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: May Allah bless me and you through the Mighty Qur’an and benefit me and you with the verses and the wise reminder it contains. I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
